title: DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Each worker objective fᵢ is convex and differentiable on ℝᵈ. The mean objective F is convex and has an L-Lipschitz gradient. The stated smoothness bound applies to F.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with n ≥ 1 and one hidden component function assigned to each computing worker.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, Params.n, Functions, objective, spec.Instance, and spec.admissible

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A completed evaluation at worker i returns its query point x and a sample gᵢ(x,ξ) with mean ∇fᵢ(x). The sample law may depend on i. The functions, oracle maps, and sample laws are hidden. All Params fields are public, including x₀, d, n, h, l, b, L, μ, ρ, R, σ, and ε.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.unbiased. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, ComputeReply and computation

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i can sample the gradient of its assigned fᵢ at a requested point. Node 0 coordinates communication and has no gradient oracle.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, (1/n)∑ᵢ‖∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ ρ‖∇F(x)‖², with ρ ≥ 1. This bounds the true worker gradients. At every minimizer of F, all true worker gradients vanish, while stochastic samples may still have positive variance.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every worker and query point, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ)−∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σ², with σ ≥ 0. Each worker uses an i.i.d. sample stream, and the entire streams are independent across workers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: Writing X* = argmin F, there is a z ∈ X* with ‖x₀−z‖ ≤ R, and F(x)−F(z) ≥ (μ/2)dist(x,X*)² for every x. The parameters satisfy 0 < μ ≤ L and R ≥ 0. Multiple minimizers are permitted.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain and output space are ℝᵈ with the Euclidean norm, for a public natural number d.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Worker i takes a fixed time hᵢ > 0 per evaluation and can have one pending evaluation. Workers and directed star links can operate concurrently, with one message in flight per direction per link. A k-bit payload takes l + b(k + 64) time, including the clock overhead, with l,b ≥ 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, Network, computation, and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits, and step

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: The designated output node returns a measurable point X at the elapsed-time deadline. Its error is the squared Euclidean distance to the full solution set, dist(X,argmin F)².
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, solutions and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The squared distance must be integrable and satisfy E[dist(X,argmin F)²] ≤ ε for ε > 0. Expectation is over the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws. The time budget is fixed by the public parameters, and execution must have finitely many events almost surely through that deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents, and TimedConvergence

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines quadratic growth of the mean objective and a relative bound on true worker gradients with persistent sampling noise. It measures time to expected squared solution-set distance on a star with unequal worker speeds, concurrent directed links, message latency, and per-bit charges.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Minimization Under Strong Growth

We minimize the mean of differentiable convex functions on Rd, where d is a nonnegative integer. The mean has a Lipschitz gradient and satisfies quadratic growth away from its minimizer set. The average squared norm of the local gradients is bounded by a constant times the squared norm of the mean gradient. A given starting point lies within a prescribed radius of a minimizer. On a star network, each worker returns an unbiased stochastic local gradient with bounded variance using independent samples. By the elapsed-time deadline, the output must have expected squared distance to the minimizer set at most ε, for a given tolerance ε>0.

For n≥1 workers with local objectives fi:Rd→R, define F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x). The problem is minx∈RdF(x). Write S=argminx∈RdF(x) and dist(x,S)=infz∈S∥x−z∥, using the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives d, n, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈Rd, the network parameters (hi)i=1n,ℓ,b, and the constants L,μ,ρ,R,σ,ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Local convexity and mean smoothness). Each fi is convex and differentiable on Rd. For every x,y∈Rd, ∥∇F(x)−∇F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Strong growth of local gradients). For ρ≥1 and every x∈Rd, 1n∑i=1n∥∇fi(x)∥2≤ρ∥∇F(x)∥2.

Assumption 3 (Quadratic growth and initial distance). For 0<μ≤L and R≥0, there exists x⋆∈S such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and, for every x∈Rd, F(x)−F(x⋆)≥μ2dist(x,S)2.

Assumption 4 (Stochastic local gradients). Worker i has a jointly measurable map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd and a sequence of measurable samples (ξi,k)k≥0 that are independent with common probability law νi. The sequences are independent across workers, and the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample array. At any query point x∈Rd, the worker’s (k+1)st completed evaluation returns (x,gi(x,ξi,k)). For ξ∼νi, the vector gi(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and its squared error is integrable. For every i and x, with σ≥0, Eξ∼νi[gi(x,ξ)]=∇fi(x),Eξ∼νi[∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σ2.

A central node connects to each worker, and only the workers evaluate stochastic gradients. An evaluation at worker i takes hi>0 time. Each worker handles one evaluation at a time, ignores new evaluation requests while busy, and can abort a pending evaluation without consuming a sample. Messages travel in either direction along a star edge. A payload of m≥0 bits is transmitted with 64 trailing zero bits and takes ℓ+b(m+64) time, where ℓ≥0 is the latency and b≥0 is the time per bit. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the transmitted bits. Each directed link carries one message at a time and ignores submissions while occupied. Distinct directed links can operate concurrently, including opposite directions on the same edge, and communication can overlap with computation.

Let T≥0 be the elapsed-time budget. Almost surely over the samples and the algorithm’s randomness, only finitely many events may occur for every deadline t∈[0,T]. At time T, the algorithm’s designated output node must produce a measurable point x¯∈Rd with integrable squared distance to S satisfying E[dist(x¯,S)2]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, the n local losses fi are differentiable and convex. Their mean F is L-smooth and satisfies μ-quadratic growth to S=arg⁡minF, with 0<μ≤L and dist(x0,S)≤R. Mean strong growth is ∑i∥∇fi(x)∥2≤nρ∥∇F(x)∥2 for ρ≥1. Jointly measurable unbiased stochastic gradients have variance at most σ2, with IID samples within workers and independent streams across workers. Workers compute in parallel, one gradient at a time, taking hi>0 per gradient. Only hub–worker links carry messages, at most one in flight per directed link, with latency ℓ and time b per bit. The output satisfies E[dist(X,S)2]≤ε for ε>0.

Elapsed-time upper bounds under distributed mean strong growth
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) DistributedStrongGrowthTime (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(σ2/(μ2Iε)+AnJBn)
(2) DistributedGradientDiversity (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(σ2/(μ2Iε)+ADJBD)
(3) Malenia SGD (Tyurin 2026, Thm. F.2) O([HLμ+σ2∑ihin2μ2ε]J) (1), (2): At ℓ=b=0, reduce the noise term by a factor I(∑ihi)J/n2. The speed factor is strict for unequal speeds and ρ<n∑ihi2/(∑ihi)2. With fixed n>2, times 1,…,1,H, ρ=2, ε=H−2, and other parameters fixed, O(H3log⁡H)→O(H2). Covers Remark 2.4’s pointwise condition under convexity and quadratic growth. For m unit-time workers plus times 1,…,m, ρ=2, ε=m−11/4, and other parameters fixed, (2) gives O(m11/4/log⁡m) versus O(m11/4log⁡m). (1), (2): Need ρ and known hi. The common comparison uses aggregate PL from convex quadratic growth. At ℓ=b=0, the noiseless term costs at least n times more for (1). At equal speeds and ρ=2, (2) narrows the overhead from order n to n when rounds dominate.
(4) Rennala SGD (Tyurin 2026, Thm. 3.8) O(Jmin1≤m≤nmLmax/μloc+σ2/(εμloc2)∑i≤mh(i)−1) (1), (2): Scope extends to workers without individual smoothness assumptions, local PL, or identical minimizer sets. Compare only with these three restrictions and ℓ=b=0. (1), (2): Require bounded mean strong growth. On identical losses with ρ=1 and free communication, (1) pays at least an n-fold noiseless overhead.

Abbr: H=maxihi, S=∑ihi−1, and J=1+log⁡(1+R2/ε). The profile u minimizes ∑iui2/hi subject to ∑iui=n and ∑iui2≤nρ. Set I=∑iui2/hi, U=maxiui, W=maxiui/hi, D=max{min(n,1+n(ρ−1)),nW/(US)}, Aq=qLUS/(μI), and Bq=H+ℓ+b[1+dlog⁡(2+d+Aq+(R2+σ2/(q2L2))/ε)]. Here h(i) are the times in increasing order, Lmax is the maximum local smoothness constant, and μloc is the common local PL constant.

import LongTails.Setups.DistributedWeakInterpolation

open MeasureTheory DistributedTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedMeanStrongGrowth

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ+
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  h : Fin n → Time
  l : Time
  b : Time
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ
abbrev Samples (p : Params) := Fin p.n → ℕ → p.Ω

noncomputable def objective (p : Params) (f : Functions p) (x : Point p) := (∑ i, f i x) / p.n

def solutions (p : Params) (f : Functions p) := {x | IsMinOn (objective p f) Set.univ x}

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  publicInput := id
  numWorkers p := p.n + 1
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery p := StarNetwork.ComputeQuery (Point p)
  ComputeReply p := StarNetwork.ComputeReply (Point p) (Point p)
  CommReply p := StarNetwork.CommReply p.n
  Output := Point
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 1 ≤ p.ρ ∧
    0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i) ∧ ∀ x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient (objective p f) x - gradient (objective p f) y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x-y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, ∑ i, ‖gradient (f i) x‖ ^ 2 ≤ p.n * p.ρ * ‖gradient (objective p f) x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∃ z ∈ solutions p f, ‖p.x0-z‖ ≤ p.R ∧ ∀ x,
      p.μ / 2 * Metric.infDist x (solutions p f)^2 ≤ objective p f x - objective p f z) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (ν : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)),
      O = StarNetwork.system ⟨p.h,p.l,p.b⟩ (fun i x (s : Samples p) k => g i x (s i k)) P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k)
        (ν i : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
        StochasticSmoothAndConvex.IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (ν i) (f i) (g i) p.σ
  successful p f output P := Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun s => Metric.infDist (output s) (solutions p f)^2) (P : Measure _) ∧
    ∫ s, Metric.infDist (output s) (solutions p f)^2 ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedMeanStrongGrowth
